title: How Do Behavioral Approaches to Increase Savings Compare? Evidence from Multiple Interventions in the U.S. Army
eligible_reason: Interventions 1-2 are RCTs (OLS on treatment dummy). Active choice (Table 3 col 4) is a cross-sectional DiD: reg y treat treatment_time treatment_location + individual covariates, i.e., a pooled treated-location dummy (Fort Bragg/Fort Lewis) with one common treatment-window indicator, no unit or time FE. Automatic enrollment (col 5) is a single-date (Jan 1, 2018) DiD against the prior-year cohort. No staggered adoption; covariates in every column.
design_notes: HowDoBehavioralApproachesComparePrimarySampleManagementScience.do line 191: reg ever_tsp treat treatment_time treatment_location $controls if active_choice_sample==1, vce(cluster location_month). Event-study figures (Figures 1-2) also single-date.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Active choice: common treatment window indicator (Mar 14-Apr 14, 2016) for two bases pooled; automatic enrollment: single date Jan 1, 2018.
data_files_note: README: restricted Army OEMA administrative data, not shareable; package ships only .do files, logs and a data dictionary.
